sections.h2: Where do I take a deed in Trenton, and what are the hours?
sections.html:
The office is at 101 Market Street in Trenton, with a mailing address of PO Box 189, Trenton, NC 28585, and the phone number is 252-448-2551. Staff are at the counter Monday to Thursday from morning to late afternoon, though documents stop being accepted for recording at 4:30. Fridays are short: open from 8 a.m. to noon, with 11:30 as the recording cutoff.

That short Friday matters for a closing. A deed that reaches the counter after 11:30 on a Friday is not recorded until the next open day, which is Monday, so sellers in Jones County usually schedule signing early in the week.

The office describes its job as recording and keeping births, deaths, marriages, service discharges, notaries, assumed names, maps and real estate transactions. Its real estate indexes reach back to the late 1700s, and a search for records before 1978 has its own page on the county site.

sections.h2: How much will Jones County charge me to record the deed?
sections.html:
Trenton posts a deed at $26.00 covering page 15 and under, adding $4.00 for each later sheet; the county schedule is dated October 1, 2016. A deed of trust has a longer base of 35 pages at $64.00.

The schedule also lists the excise stamp, at $2.00 for each $1,000 of purchase price. Its information page says $1.00 per $500 of consideration, which comes to the same figure.

sections.h2: Does Jones County require tax office approval before a deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Yes. The register's page says every deed, together with a completed Tax Certification Form, must be presented to the Tax Office for approval before the document can be recorded. The form is also called the Tax Data Sheet or Tax Collection Form, and the register's site links to it.

Two more local rules sit alongside that step:

  • Under a Jones County ordinance, every deed must show the tax parcel ID number on its first page.
  • A resolution under G.S. 161-31, effective September 1, 2007, bars the register from accepting a deed for real property that is subject to delinquent taxes.

So an unpaid Jones County tax bill can stop a deed at the counter. A seller with back taxes should plan to pay them at or before closing, using the closing agent to settle the bill so the deed is accepted the same day.

sections.h2: Which recording standards apply to a Jones County deed?
sections.html:
Paper filed from July 1, 2002 forward must meet the layout standards in G.S. 161-14(b), and the Jones County register lists them on its site. A document that falls short triggers the $25.00 nonstandard document fee in addition to the usual recording fee.

  • Sheets sized 8 1/2 by 11 or by 14.
  • Three blank inches above the text on page one, half an inch on page one's other edges, and half an inch all around on the pages behind it.
  • Dark ink on white paper in a type size of at least 10 points.
  • Printing that appears on one side of the sheet only.
  • The kind of instrument named just under the top margin, and the preparer named on page one.

The register may waive the nonstandard fee if the print is smaller than 10 point but still legible once scanned. Maps and plats follow separate rules: they must be 18 by 24 inches, with one mylar and one paper copy, and a Jones County review officer must approve the map before it is recorded.

sections.h2: How do liens and satisfactions work in Jones County?
sections.html:
An old mortgage is cleared by recording a satisfaction, and the Jones County register charges nothing for it. Two kinds exist: a Satisfaction of Security Instrument signed by the secured creditor, and a Trustee's Satisfaction signed by a trustee or substitute trustee. The county notes that satisfaction by presentation ended October 1, 2011.

Wills are not recorded at the register. They go to the Jones County Clerk of Court in Trenton, which a seller handling an inherited house should know before heading to the wrong counter.

Under state law a tax lien reaches the parcel as of its January 1 listing date, bringing penalties, interest and costs with it, and an unpaid lien is enforced through a foreclosure action in court. Before you sign a sales contract, get a current payoff figure from the Jones County tax office.

sections.h2: What do I need to know about Jones County property tax before selling?
sections.html:
Jones County taxes are due September 1, and they are treated as delinquent on January 6, when interest of 2 percent for January applies, then 3/4 percent each month after. A mailed payment counts by its U.S. Postal postmark, and a postage meter date is not accepted.

Jones County last revalued on January 1, 2022, with the following revaluation set for January 1, 2030. Market changes between those dates are not counted. A seller who disagrees with an assessment can call 252-448-2546 to set up an informal appeal before March 1, and later appeals may need a formal hearing before the county review board.

Find the tax office at 418 Hwy 58 N in Trenton, where the counter shuts at five o'clock Monday through Thursday and at midday on Friday. Partial payments are taken at the Tax Collections Office, and a payment plan is available only if no enforced collection action has begun. Agricultural and forest tracts can qualify for use value taxation, and a new application goes to the assessor in the regular January listing period.

sections.h2: What does the Jones County housing market look like?
sections.html:
Few counties in the state are as thinly settled. The Census Bureau puts Jones County at 9,575 people for July 1, 2025, below the 10,153 counted in 2010, with 4,804 housing units over 471.37 square miles. In 2020 that meant 19.5 people per square mile.

Survey figures for 2020 through 2024 show a middle-of-the-market owned home at $130,300, and owners occupy 79.4 percent of them. Renters pay a median $747, and households earn a median $59,641. Residents 65 and older are 26.8 percent of the county, so many sales here involve an older owner or an estate.

Construction is slow, with 46 building permits shown for 2025. Fewer new homes on the market means a Jones County seller competes mostly with other resales, and a house that needs repairs can sit for a long time.

sections.h2: Does a cash sale change the recording steps in Jones County?
sections.html:
A cash buyer's deed travels the usual route. It clears the tax office, carries the parcel number on page one, has its stamp paid by the seller, and reaches the register ahead of the weekday or Friday cutoff.

The difference is pace and condition. A cash deal skips the lender appraisal, and the house is bought in its current state. That can help an owner who has liens, a vacant house, tenants or an estate to wind up. Overdue taxes must still be cleared at closing so the register will take the deed.

faqs.q: What are the Jones County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: Monday through Thursday it opens at 8 a.m. and closes at 5 p.m., but the last recording is taken at 4:30 p.m. Friday hours run from 8 a.m. to noon, with the last recording at 11:30 a.m. The phone is 252-448-2551.

faqs.q: Can Jones County record a deed if property taxes are unpaid?
faqs.a: No. A resolution under G.S. 161-31, effective September 1, 2007, bars the register from accepting a deed for property subject to delinquent taxes. Pay the bill first, then present the deed.

faqs.q: What must page one of a Jones County deed show?
faqs.a: The tax parcel ID number, as required by a county ordinance, plus the type of instrument and the preparer's name. A 3 inch top margin and 1/2 inch side margins also apply.

faqs.q: Does Jones County bill for recording a loan release?
faqs.a: No. The county lists a satisfaction of a deed of trust as free, and that holds for either type, the creditor's signed form or the trustee's.

faqs.q: Where are wills recorded in Jones County?
faqs.a: At the Jones County Clerk of Court in Trenton, phone 252-448-6220, not at the Register of Deeds. The register records the deeds that follow.
